chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who takes wine and makes it into vinegar. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem'.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is wine that turns into vinegar considered halal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* through the chain of prominent companions like Ubayd ibn Zurara, this hadith clarifies the juristic principle of *istihlak* (transformation), confirming that wine's intoxicating nature is lost when it becomes vinegar, rendering it pure (*tahir*) and permissible (*halal*). This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between the original state of *khamr* and its transformed state, often linked to the Quranic verse on the gradual prohibition of intoxicants.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhamad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who took the wine and made it into vinegar. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who takes wine and turns it into vinegar. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
